map.五级浓度分级与处置：<0.5% 安全（正常作业、持续监测）、0.5%~0.8%: Five concentration levels and responses: <0.5% safe (normal work, continuous monitoring), 0.5%~0.8% caution (increase ventilation and monitoring frequency), 0.8%~1.0% alert (stop part of the work, evacuate non-essential personnel), 1.0%~1.5% danger (stop work, cut power, withdraw personnel), ≥1.5% extremely dangerous (evacuate immediately, seal the working face, report for handling).
map.断电阈值：浓度达到或超过 1.0% 即判需立即切断电源；页面按监测位置（工作面/: Power-cut threshold: a concentration reaching or exceeding 1.0% means power must be cut immediately; the page labels the measuring point by monitoring location (working face / return airflow, general roadway, near electrical equipment), and the threshold at all three is 1.0%.
map.爆炸性判定：浓度落在 5%~16% 区间判为处于爆炸浓度范围（极度危险）；低于: Explosibility judgement: a concentration falling in the 5%~16% range is judged to be within the explosive concentration range (extremely dangerous); below 5% it is under the lower explosive limit and will not explode; above 16% it is above the upper explosive limit and will not explode because of oxygen deficiency. The page uses a five-segment colour bar (safe green / caution blue / alert yellow / danger red / extreme-danger dark red) to show which range the current concentration falls in.

map.为什么规定瓦斯浓度达到 1.0% 就要断电撤人？: Why must power be cut and personnel withdrawn when the gas concentration reaches 1.0%?
map.1.0% 远低于 5% 的爆炸下限，留出的余量用于应对监测滞后、局部积聚与浓度快: 1.0% is far below the 5% lower explosive limit, and the margin allows for monitoring lag, local accumulation and rapid concentration rises. Gas distribution underground is highly uneven, and local high concentrations easily form at the roof, in corners and in unventilated areas, so when a measuring point reads 1.0% the local value may already be far higher. The regulations therefore require stopping work, cutting power and withdrawing personnel at 1.0%, then ventilating and re-testing until acceptable before resuming, rather than waiting until the concentration approaches the lower explosive limit.
map.浓度超过 16% 反而「不爆炸」，是不是就不危险了？: If the concentration exceeds 16% it "does not explode" — does that mean it is no longer dangerous?
map.不是。高于爆炸上限只是意味着该处混合气体因缺氧而无法被点燃，但极其危险：一是人员: No. Being above the upper explosive limit only means the mixture at that point cannot be ignited because of oxygen deficiency, but it is extremely dangerous: first, anyone entering will suffocate from lack of oxygen; second, once the gas mixes with fresh air and is diluted back into the 5%~16% range it immediately becomes an explosive mixture. Accumulations of high-concentration gas must therefore be sealed and kept strictly off-limits; they are handled by a professional rescue team following gas drainage procedures with slow release and continuous monitoring of the concentration in the return airflow.

Whether the explosion triangle exists also depends on oxygen (a common criterion is ≥12%) and an ignition source. Oxygen may be left blank; the page then does not assert explosible or non-explosible.

map.为什么不能只看一个 1.0% 阈值就下结论？: Why can’t I conclude from a single 1.0% threshold?
map.不同地区、工况、巷道类型与设备类别的报警、撤人、断电要求可能不同，现场还受测点代: Alarm, evacuation and power-cut requirements can differ by region, condition, roadway type and equipment class. On site, measurement representativeness, ventilation, oxygen and ignition sources also matter. The page makes thresholds configurable and labels them as examples for professionals to set under the applicable code; the result is a reference classification, not an enforcement or response basis.
map.浓度高于 16% 是不是就不爆炸、可以进入？: Does methane above 16% mean no explosion and safe entry?
map.绝对不能。高于爆炸上限只说明该混合气在当前氧含量下可能无法被点燃，但高浓度瓦斯可: Absolutely not. Above the upper explosive limit only means the mixture may not ignite at the current oxygen level; high methane can still cause asphyxiation, and mixing with fresh air may bring it back into 5%–16% and form an explosive mixture. Seal the area, evacuate, and let a professional rescue team handle it while monitoring the return airway.

Defaults 0.5%/1.0% are examples only; qualified professionals must set and review them for the region, conditions and current code. 5%–16% is only the methane explosive range; explosion conditions also depend on oxygen (commonly ≥12%) and an ignition source, and one reading cannot represent the whole section.

Below 5%, concentration alone cannot establish safety (local accumulation or measurement error is possible); above 16%, concentration alone cannot establish “will not ignite” or “will not asphyxiate” — high methane can cause oxygen deficiency, and dilution back to 5%–16% may form an explosive mixture, so treat as high risk.
map.瓦斯爆炸三角需同时具备：浓度 5%~16% + 氧气 ≥12% + 点火源达到引: The methane explosion triangle requires all three: concentration 5%–16% + oxygen ≥12% + an ignition source at ignition temperature. Missing any one does not establish safety; mixing, pressure and temperature also matter.
